sentences.text:
Manoj Malviya - learned counsel for the appellants  Shri Manoj Jain, learned counsel for the respondent No.
 ORDER

This Miscellaneous Appeal has been preferred under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the impugned award dated 30/07/2015 passed by Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Neemuch (M.P.) in Claim Case No.132/2013, whereby an amount of Rs.6,54,600/-
has been awarded from the date of filing of claim petition the appellants / claimants / survivors of the deceased Smt. Devkishan Gyari with interest @ 8% per annum, who died in the accident occurred on 23.1.2013.

entities.text: Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Neemuch (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellants / survivors of the deceased submits that the learned Claims Tribunal has erred in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.4,500/- per month only.
He submits that the learned tribunal has not considered the future prospects properly.
He NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8519 2 MA-2291-2015 submits that the deceased was working as a labourer.

His contention is that in case the income of the deceased is not proved by any cogent evidence, income ought to have been assessed on the basis of circular issued by Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh under the Minimum Wages Act, according to which income of the deceased on the date of accident comes to Rs.4,945/- per month.

entities.text: Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He further submits that the learned Claims Tribunal has awarded a meager amount of Rs.1,20,000/- in the head of Loss of Consortium and love and affection.
He submits that looking to the members of family consortium amount should be awarded to all the members/claimants.

His contention is that all the survivors should have been awarded Rs.40,000/-
each in the head of Loss of Consortium in the light of para 59.8 of the judgment delivered in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

Learned Claims Tribunal has also not awarded just and proper amount in head of Loss of Estate,
therefore, an amount of Rs.15,000/- is to be added in this head.

Learned counsel further submits that learned Claims Tribunal has erred in not awarding any amount in the head of future prospects, whereas as per para 59.4 of Pranay Sethi (Supra), looking to the age 48 years of the deceased, 25% amount is to be added in the head of Future Prospects.
The other aspects and points are not in dispute and hence learned counsel prays for allowing the appeal by enhancing the award amount.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8519 3 MA-2291-2015
Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / Insurance Company has opposed the prayer on the ground that evidence led before the learned Claims Tribunal has been rightly appreciated.
The amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required.
All the factors have been considered by the learned Claims Tribunal while awarding the compensation amount and no fault can be found with in the impugned award.
He also submits that the learned claims tribunal has awarded the rate of interest @ of 8% which is on higher side therefore, the same be reduced to 6%.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the appeal being devoid of any substance.
Heard and considered the rival submissions raised at bar by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5. From perusal of the record, it is apparent that at the time of accident i.e. on 23.1.2013 deceased was working as labourer.

However, his income has not been established by adducing cogent evidence, therefore, in the light of the judgment delivered by the apex Court in the case of Chandra @ Chanda @ Chandraram & Anr. Vs. Mukesh Kumar Yadav reported in (2022) 1 SCC 198 : 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3093, income of the deceased is to be assessed on the basis of circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act, therefore, on the basis of circular income of the deceased is assessed at Rs.4945/- per month considering him as a labour.
6.

entities.text: Chandra @ Chanda @ Chandraram & Anr. Vs. Mukesh Kumar Yadav reported in (2022) 1 SCC 198 : 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3093
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Learned Claims Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.25,000/-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8519 4 MA-2291-2015 in the head of Funeral Expenses, which according to 59.8 of the judgment in the case of Pranay Sethi (Supra) is on higher side, therefore, the same is reduced from Rs.25,000/- to Rs.15,000/-.
However, since no amount has been awarded in the head of Loss of Estate, therefore, an amount of Rs.15,000/- is added in this head.
Since the survivors are five in number, therefore, they all are entitled for an amount of Rs.40,000/- each in the head of loss of consortium.
7. Deceased was 48 years of age at the time of accident, therefore, as per para 59.4 of Pranay Sethi (Supra), 25% amount is added in the head of Future Prospects.

8. Accordingly, the just and proper compensation amount comes as under:-
Dhapubai vs Gangabai on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125272336/
2 Loss of dependency Rs.6,42,850 (Rs.4945 + 25% FP - 1/3rd x 12 x 13 Loss of consortium Rs.2,00,000/-
 Funeral expenses Rs.15,000/-
 Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-
Medical bills Rs.36,600/-
Total amount Rs.9,09,450/-
Claims
tribunal award Rs.6,54,600/-
Enhanced amount Rs.2,54,850/-
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.2,54,850/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.6,45,600/-.
Accordingly, the appellants are entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.2,54,850/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
The direction of claims tribunal as regards pay and recover shall remain intact.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8519 5 MA-2291-2015 9.
Resultantly, the appeal filed by the appellants / claimants is allowed to the extent as indicated hereinabove.
10. Learned counsel for the Insurance Co. submits that the learned claims tribunal has awarded the rate of interest @ of 8% which is on higher side therefore, the same be reduced to 6%.

However in this regard, no cross objection has been filed by the learned counsel for the Insurance Co. therefore,
the rate of interest cannot be reduced.

(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE SS/-
